measurement: PYTHONPATH=infra/kiwi python3 -m traceability validate — specs + links only, no stand, no network, no test run (scripts/check-traceability-ratchet.py recomputes both numbers from the same package that renders the matrix)

floors.label: claimed (scenario, target) cells with no automation
floors.note: The number the plan asked for, and the one 15 auth/sync specs with zero carriers blew past in a single commit: 2 -> 32, green, because nothing read it. Removing a hole is always allowed; adding one fails. Raised 31 -> 32 on 2026-10-05 for one reason, recorded here because a raised floor is only defensible if the reason is in the repo: TASK-TIME-01 was narrowed to `targets: [android]` on the strength of a failed reachability probe, and the narrowing was wrong. The time-tracking feature is entirely in commonMain, and the desktop task detail was not rendering it because a merge (f2a87c7c) had put the two platform navigation graphs on different screens. The spec now claims both targets because that is true of the product, and the desktop cell is a hole because no carrier can assert it yet — the timer will not start under the anonymous desktop harness session and TaskTimeSlot.start() discards the failure with an empty onFailure, so the failure is indistinguishable from a dead control (#196). A claim that is true and unsupplied is a hole; a spec narrowed to match a bug is neither honest nor a coverage claim. Lowered 32 -> 31 on 2026-10-05 when the desktop carrier for TASK-TIME-01 landed. That cell had been open since #187 with a recorded blocker that was wrong twice: first 'the UI is Android-only' (the feature is in commonMain), then 'the harness session is Anonymous'. The real cause was a type collision — TaskDetailIntent.Domain.Start implemented the TaskTimeSlotIntent marker without being TaskTimeSlotIntent.Start, so the slot's `when` fell through to a silent `else { }` (#212). The claim was true and supplied all along.

floors.label: declared scenarios with a claimed target and no automation on any target
floors.note: A cell count cannot see a change that leaves the cell count alone while the number of scenarios in trouble goes up. Verified by brute force over every per-scenario (claimed, automated) state on both targets: 85 such trades exist, the simplest being a spec split. One scenario claiming [android, desktop] with no carrier is 2 holes and 1 dark scenario; split it per platform into two specs each claiming one target and the total is still 2 holes, but 2 dark scenarios. Splitting a spec per platform looks like tidying up, which is what makes it worth ratcheting. Lowered 16 -> 15 on 2026-10-05 when TASK-TIME-01 stopped being dark: the spec had claimed desktop for the first time (which alone would have been +1 holes and failed this gate) and the desktop carrier that landed with the fix took the total back to 31. Lowered 16 -> 15 on 2026-10-05, same commit: TASK-TIME-01 stopped being dark because its desktop cell gained a carrier, so the scenario is now automated on one target instead of neither.

floors.label: claimed cells whose spec declares the tier unable to reach them
floors.note: These are counted in `holes` as well, so reclassifying an ordinary hole as unreachable does not move the total — which is the point, and also the hole this floor closes. Without it, marking every unsupplied claim `unreachable` would make the queue look un-actionable while the number stayed at 32, and the cheap move is always the one that leaves the metric alone. The two metrics together mean a reclassification has to be paid for in one bucket or the other. The 6 are the three sync scenarios that are *defined* by a second device (SYNC-INCOMING-01, SYNC-OFFLINE-01, SYNC-PROFILES-01) on both tiers; the rest of the sync area is one-device and stays probe-able.

known_gaps: 16 android cells are holes and stay holes on a host with no device: the tier is unverifiable here, and that is more than half the matrix. docs/testing/android-tier-runbook.md is the work order. Because every android hole is 1-for-1, no desktop work can move the total by more than 1; the android tier is where the count is.
